x: UNDRR is the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction. Its old name, UNISDR, stood for UN International Strategy for Disaster Reduction.
t: Discriminate the current name from the old name.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Sendai Framework, adopted in 2015, covers 2015–2030. 2005–2015 was the Hyogo Framework. UNISDR became UNDRR on 1 May 2019.
t: Discriminate the Hyogo and Sendai periods.

x: Both are true: UNDRR is the custodian of the Sendai Framework because it supports its implementation, monitoring and review. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the work explains the custodian role.

x: 1989–1999 was the International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction, 2005 Hyogo, 2015 Sendai, and 2019 the rename to UNDRR. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Arrange the DRR milestones in time order.

x: All three are correct: understanding risk, investing in DRR, and preparedness with 'build back better' are three of Sendai's four priorities. The fourth is strengthening risk governance.
t: Recall the four Sendai priorities.

x: Both are true: UNDRR is the UN's focal point for DRR, and it is led by the Special Representative of the Secretary-General. Who leads it does not explain its role, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether leadership explains a role.

x: UNDRR coordinates DRR across the UN, advocates a culture of DRR, and supplies tools, guidelines, data and best practices. The answer is a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-v, e-ii, f-vi.
t: Match each function to its description.

x: UNDRR convenes the Global Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction, the main world forum on DRR.
t: Recall who convenes the Global Platform.

x: The Sendai Framework was adopted on 18 March 2015 at the Third UN World Conference on DRR, held in Sendai, Japan. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
t: Match each Sendai fact to its value.

x: All seven are Sendai targets: four to reduce (deaths, people affected, economic loss, infrastructure damage) and three to increase (DRR strategies, international cooperation, early warning).
t: Recall the seven Sendai targets.

x: Option A is incorrect: Sendai followed the Hyogo Framework of 2005–2015, not 2010–2020. It runs 2015–2030 under UNDRR.
t: Discriminate the Hyogo and Sendai periods.

x: Both are true: Sendai is voluntary and non-binding, and it followed Hyogo. Being a successor does not explain being non-binding, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether succession explains legal status.

x: Priority 1 is understanding risk, 2 governance, 3 investing for resilience, and 4 preparedness and building back better. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Recall the four Sendai priorities in order.

x: I and III are correct: Target C cuts economic loss relative to GDP by 2030, and Target G widens early warning by 2030. II is false because Target E's deadline was 2020, not 2030.
t: Recall that Target E alone ends in 2020.

x: Both are true: whole-of-society engagement involves government, business, civil society, academia and media, and the multi-hazard approach covers natural and man-made hazards.
t: Recall the Sendai principles.

x: All nine are in Sendai's expected outcome: reducing disaster risk and losses in lives, livelihoods and health, and in economic, physical, social, cultural and environmental assets.
t: Recall the Sendai expected outcome.

x: Both are true: understanding risk means assessing it in all its dimensions, and those dimensions are hazard, vulnerability, exposure and capacity. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the dimensions explain the assessment.

x: All four are correct: strengthening risk governance stresses laws, institutions, policies and coordination at every level.
t: Recall the governance priority.

x: Both are true: the investment priority covers both public and private spending on prevention and mitigation.
t: Recall the investment priority.

x: Preparedness, recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction all fall under Priority 4 (preparedness and building back better). The answer is a-i, b-i, c-i, d-i.
t: Allow codes to repeat.

x: Target A cuts disaster deaths, Target B people affected, and Target D damage to critical infrastructure and disruption of basic services, all by 2030. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Recall the Sendai targets by letter.

x: Target F is to greatly increase international cooperation with developing countries by 2030. C is economic loss, E is DRR strategies (by 2020), and G is early warning.
t: Recall the Sendai targets by letter.

x: Both are true: States have the main role in reducing disaster risk, because the primary responsibility of States is a Sendai principle. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the principle explains the role.

x: Both are true: 'build back better' uses recovery to reduce future risk, and the inclusive principle gives special attention to vulnerable groups.
t: Recall the Sendai principles.

x: WCDRR is the World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction. The traps swap in 'Council', 'Convention' or 'Development'.
t: Expand the short name.

x: Option C is incorrect: UNDRR (then UNISDR) coordinated the second and third WCDRRs, not the first. All three were held in Japan.
t: Recall who ran each WCDRR.

x: Both are true: Sendai is the current global DRR framework, and it runs 2015–2030. Its dates alone do not explain its status, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a period explains a status.

x: The 1st WCDRR gave the Yokohama Strategy, the 2nd the Hyogo Framework, and the 3rd the Sendai Framework. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
t: Match each WCDRR to its outcome.

x: The order is the 1st WCDRR (1994), the 2nd (2005) and the 3rd (2015). The answer is B, C, A.
t: Arrange the WCDRRs in time order.

x: The 1st WCDRR was held at Yokohama, the 2nd at Kobe (Hyogo), and the 3rd at Sendai, all in Japan. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
t: Match each WCDRR to its city.

x: All three are correct: the Yokohama Strategy (1994) gave the first global guidelines on disaster prevention, preparedness and mitigation.
t: Recall the Yokohama Strategy.

x: Both are true: Hyogo aimed to build resilient nations and communities, and it had five priorities. The number of priorities does not explain the aim, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a count explains an aim.

x: All three are correct: Sendai has four priorities and seven global targets, and includes 'build back better'.
t: Recall Sendai's 4 priorities and 7 targets.

x: World Tsunami Awareness Day is 5 November. 13 October is the DRR day, 23 March Meteorological Day, and 19 August Humanitarian Day.
t: Match each day to its date.

x: Option C is incorrect: World Environment Day is 5 June, not 15 June. The other dates are right.
t: Match each day to its date.

x: Both are true: World Meteorological Day matters for DRR because it highlights weather, climate and water services that support warnings. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the theme explains the relevance.

x: All three are correct: NDMA was notified in 2006, NDRF raised in 2006, and NDMA, NIDM, NDRF and the States hold drills and campaigns all year.
t: Recall the 2006 milestones.

x: Earth Day (22 April) concerns environmental protection, World Environment Day links environmental damage with disaster risk, IDDRR is the main DRR day, and the WMO declared Meteorological Day. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Match each day to its theme.

x: All five are correct: the UN declared both days; Tsunami Day (since 2015) was inspired by Japan's 'Inamura-no-hi' story, and Humanitarian Day honours aid workers and people hit by crises.
t: Recall the UN days.

x: Both are true: the UN declared the International Day for DRR, and it has been observed since 1989. Its start year does not explain why it was declared, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a date explains a declaration.

x: Both are true: NDMA Formation Day falls around 26–27 September, and NDRF Raising Day on 19 January.
t: Recall the Indian DRR days.

x: The International Day for DRR (13 October) promotes a global culture of risk reduction and resilience. The other options are the tsunami, humanitarian and meteorological days.
t: Match each day to its theme.
